title: Limit Your Inputs
coreMove: Guard your mind at the door: ask what is necessary, filter work before it becomes duty, and let fewer inputs earn the deeper attention they deserve.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who confuse alerts with guidance
exampleSpecs.stakes: transit news can crowd out the one sign that matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use the bus depot bench to reveal that extra alerts hid the necessary cue

exampleSpecs.stakes: a stray message can become a needless practice change
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use the sports field sideline as a compressed message exchange that filters chaff

exampleSpecs.stakes: one buzz can turn a useful chore into scattered attention
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use the pantry shelf interruption to show the pause as the filtering technique

exampleSpecs.audience: readers sorting requests in a noisy setting
exampleSpecs.stakes: a calm bench can separate useful updates from stray wants
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use the baseball dugout bench as a close observed moment without a forced decision

exampleSpecs.audience: readers reviewing how noise became work
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed tray shows how unfiltered requests multiply
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: open after the outcome and reconstruct the intake failure from evidence

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who notice their own distraction mid-task
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small input error can become a safety problem
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use the electrical panel room to center the moment of noticing an input mistake
